park: Jardi Botanic de la Universitat de Valencia
name: the Jardi Botanic
title: Ancient Trees in Valencia's Jardi Botanic: 8 to Find
meta_description: Bhutan's national tree, a Caucasian elm shaped like a bundle of branches, a pine that never leaned. Eight monumental trees in Valencia's university garden.
intro: Valencia's university botanic garden moved to this walled plot off Carrer Quart in 1802, and eight of the city's monumental trees now stand inside it, more than any other single place in Valencia. The Kashmir cypress is Bhutan's national tree, kept alive around Buddhist temples for centuries before Western botany even named it. The Caucasian elm grows nothing like an elm, its trunk breaking early into a sheaf of near-vertical branches that reads more like a bundle than a canopy. A Turkish pine went straight up for thirty metres without leaning or forking once, while a silk floss tree, a southern live oak, a Hartwiss oak, a London plane and a river she-oak fill out a collection assembled from four continents. Most of these carry no recorded planting date: the garden's own register measures trunks and crowns but keeps no year, so age here is mostly an open question left for whoever can read a ring count. The garden charges a small admission fee and is open to the public.
